title: HNSW search: long jumps on the upper layers, a wide search on layer 0
caption: Fourteen nodes and one question. Every node keeps its place on every layer, and every distance is measured from the question.

frames.title: Layer 2: from entry point E to K
frames.note: Upper layers hold few nodes, so each move goes far. K, a neighbour of E, is closer to the question, so the walk moves there. No neighbour of K is closer, so it goes down to K on the layer below.

frames.title: Layer 1: move from K to M
frames.note: Of K's neighbours E, G and M, M is the closest. No neighbour of M is closer than M, so the walk goes down at M.

frames.title: Layer 0: keep the 3 closest neighbours of M (ef=3)
frames.note: Layer 0 holds every node. Here the search keeps ef candidates instead of one. Of M's five neighbours, H, J and D stay in the list, and L and K are dropped.

frames.title: Layer 0: N joins the list, D drops out
frames.note: H has no new neighbour. J's neighbour N is closer than D, the farthest in the list, so N comes in and D drops out.

frames.title: End of layer 0: no candidate can get closer, the answer is N
frames.note: N's neighbour I is farther than J, the farthest in the list, so it stays out. The last candidate, D, is farther than J too, so the search stops. N, the closest in the list, is the answer.

frames.title: Compare: with one candidate (ef=1) the walk stops at H and misses N
frames.note: From M the walk moves to H, the closest neighbour. H's neighbours M and D are both farther than H, so it stops. N can be reached only through J, which is farther than H. A larger ef finds more but takes longer.
